thread.title: Amazon’s Amazing Stock Rocket Ride in 2018 (So Far)

author: Jon Swartz
title: Amazon’s Amazing Stock Rocket Ride in 2018 (So Far)
text:
Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos Illustration: David Ryder/Getty Images It may sound like a broken record, but Amazon.com (AMZN) continues to just do that: Break records.
Today's triumph? Its shares topped $1,500 for the second day in a row, briefly touching $1,502.54 before settling at $1,485.34, up $2.42 per share today. The company, now valued at $719.1 billion, trails only Apple (AAPL) and Alphabet (GOOGL).
Amazon's bullish gallop this year—its stock is up 27% despite a historic market correction—started with eye-popping financial results earlier this month, when it reported a profit of nearly $1.9 billion, the largest in its 23-year history. Amazon went public in 1997.
Its strong start to 2018 carries over from 2017, when its stock soared 73% and shares hit $1,000 in May. The surge in price has made Amazon founder Jeff Bezos , with $100 billion in wealth, the richest man on Earth.
We can probably expect more of the same in 2018 as Amazon finalizes plans to add a second headquarters in the U.S., muscles its way into the grocery industry with its $13 billion acquisition of Whole Foods Market , builds a highly profitable cloud-computing business, and delves into health care via a partnership with Warren Buffett and Jaime Dimon .
